source.title: SAC: Disaggregated KV Cache System for Sparse Attention LLMs with CXL
source.summary: The scaling of LLMs toward long-context inference has shifted the primary serving system bottleneck from computation to memory capacity. Traditional solutions for dense attention models rely on RDMA-based disaggregated memory pools, which perform coarse-grained fetching of the entire prefix KV cache from remote storage to local memory before decoding. However, this approach is fundamentally inefficient for emerging sparse attention models. While only a small fraction of KV entries are active during decoding, these systems still fetch the full KV cache locally, leading to severe transmission bottlenecks and local memory wastage. To address this, we propose SAC, the first efficient disaggregated KV cache system optimized for sparse attention models. By leveraging the low-latency, cache-line granularity load/store semantics of Compute Express Link (CXL), SAC fetches only the required top-k KV entries on demand during inference. Evaluations on DeepSeek-V3.2 using SGLang show that SAC achieves 2.1x higher throughput, 9.7x lower TTFT, and 1.8x lower TBT compared to RDMA-based baselines, establishing CXL-based disaggregation as the superior infrastructure for emerging sparse attention models.

previous_facts.title: SAC: Disaggregated KV Cache System for Sparse Attention LLMs with CXL
previous_facts.event_hint: SAC (Sparse Attention on CXL): first CXL-based disaggregated KV cache system for sparse attention LLM serving (DeepSeek-V3.2 on SGLang).
previous_facts.problem: Traditional RDMA-based disaggregated KV cache pools (e.g., MoonCake, LMCache) full-fetch the entire prefix KV cache from remote to local memory before decoding. For sparse attention models (DeepSeek Sparse Attention, top-k=2048 per layer), only a small fraction of KV entries are active per layer, so full-fetching wastes transmission bandwidth (transmission bottleneck P1: dozens-of-seconds latency at high concurrency on 100 Gbps RNIC) and wastes local memory (P2: only 21% of KV cache utilized at 128K context; DeepSeek-V3.2 needs 9.2 GB/request at 128K, requiring TB-level local memory for high concurrency). RDMA's message-based send/recv semantics also impose per-request software-stack overhead that accumulates across all attention layers for fine-grained top-k reads.
previous_facts.mechanism: SAC replaces RDMA with a CXL-based disaggregated KV cache pool exposing hardware-managed load/store semantics at cache-line granularity, accessed through a CXL switch (CXL 2.0/3.0, Type-3 memory devices). Built on the HiSparse framework inside SGLang, the decode instance computes top-k indices per attention layer at runtime and uses an optimized Swap-in CUDA kernel (miss identification + LRU eviction + page-table update + fetch) to fetch only the required top-k KV entries directly from the CXL memory pool into GPU HBM on demand; newly generated token KV is written back to CXL. The CXL system maps all KV data into a global CXL address space shared across compute instances, with device initialization, optimized read/write kernels, and device interleaving across multiple CXL memory devices. Prefill instance writes full KV blocks to the CXL pool after prefill.

evidence.claim: On DeepSeek-V3.2 end-to-end serving via SGLang across context lengths 16K-128K, SAC achieves 2.1x higher throughput, 9.7x lower TTFT and 1.8x lower TBT compared with an RDMA-based disaggregated memory pool baseline.
evidence.condition: DeepSeek-V3.2 on SGLang, context lengths 16K-128K, decode instance

evidence.claim: Compared with a non-disaggregated upper bound, SAC incurs only a 9% throughput degradation, which the authors use to argue CXL-based disaggregation is architecturally superior for sparse attention models.
evidence.value: 9% throughput degradation vs non-disaggregated upper bound
evidence.condition: DeepSeek-V3.2 on SGLang, same context-length range

evidence.claim: For DeepSeek-V3.2 serving 128K-context ShareGPT requests with 1K-token output, only 21% of the KV cache is actually utilized during decoding while the per-request KV footprint is 9.2 GB.
evidence.value: 21% KV utilization at 128K context; 9.2 GB KV per request at 128K
evidence.baseline: full prefix KV cache fetched locally
evidence.source_locator: PDF Page 4 (Figure 4, Section 3.1 P2: Local Memory Wasting)

evidence.claim: DeepSeek Sparse Attention uses a Lightning Indexer to score historical KV via low-dim projections and selects top-k=2048 KV latent vectors per layer for Multi-head Latent Attention, reducing attention cost from O(L^2) to O(kL).
evidence.value: top-k = 2048 KV latent vectors per layer; O(L^2) -> O(kL)
evidence.source_locator: PDF Page 2-3 (Section 2.1 Sparse Attention in LLMs, Figure 1)

evidence.claim: Microbenchmark of sparse KV retrieval latency shows CXL access latency close to DRAM and far below RDMA as the number of fetched KV indices grows from 64 to 2048 (RDMA latency explodes up to ~19.7x relative at 2048 indices while DRAM/CXL stay near flat).
evidence.value: RDMA up to ~19.7x relative latency vs ~1.04-1.04x for DRAM/CXL at 2048 indices
evidence.condition: synthetic sparse KV read microbenchmark, 64-2048 fetched indices
evidence.source_locator: PDF Page 4 (Figure 5: Retrieval latency comparison for sparse KV)

previous_facts.evaluation_context: Workload: DeepSeek-V3.2 end-to-end LLM serving integrated into SGLang, context lengths 16K-128K, ShareGPT dataset with 1K-token output, high-concurrency decode. Hardware topology: GPU compute instances plus CPU servers connected through PCIe 5.0 x16 (64 GB/s) to a CXL Switch Chip with multiple CXL-MEM devices (CXL 2.0/3.0 Type-3, cache-line-granularity load/store). Baselines: RDMA-based disaggregated pool (100 Gbps RNIC, MoonCake/LMCache-style CPU-driven RDMA bounce-buffer model) and a non-disaggregated local-memory upper bound. Microbenchmarks separately profile sparse-KV read latency for DRAM vs CXL vs RDMA across 64-2048 fetched indices.
previous_facts.limitations: Headline end-to-end speedups (2.1x throughput, 9.7x TTFT, 1.8x TBT) are reported against an RDMA pool baseline and a 9% degradation vs a non-disaggregated upper bound, but the Evidence Pack does not expose the exact concurrency level, batch size, GPU model, CXL device count/capacity, or absolute TTFT/TBT/throughput numbers behind these ratios. RDMA microbenchmark latencies are shown as relative multiples without absolute microsecond values per index count. Whether the CXL switch/memory devices are real CXL 3.0 hardware or an emulation/simulator is not stated in the visible evidence. Energy, cost-per-token and CPU utilization impact are not quantified.
previous_facts.project_relevance: Directly on-topic for the memory-semantics/DSA card: SAC is a concrete case of changing the memory sharing/placement/remote-access semantics (CXL cache-line-granularity load/store replacing RDMA message semantics) and demonstrating that the fine-grained memory-semantic advantage propagates to end-to-end LLM serving throughput/TTFT/TBT for a real sparse-attention model. It validates the project's question of whether micro-level memory-semantic gains conduct to end-to-end AI data-path metrics. Verification gap: confirm whether the CXL fabric is emulated and obtain absolute latency/concurrency/CPU-utilization numbers before claiming a deployable win.
